  (B) What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing, reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it)?
  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

I’m a relatively new Zerodha user, and I really appreciate the clean UI and smooth order execution — that’s what made me choose Zerodha.
 However, I feel one important feature is missing: UPI AutoPay for stock SIPs. Upstox already offers this, and it makes the SIP experience fully automatic without any risk of bank penalties. It also deducts the approximate amount based on the latest stock price, instead of requiring us to add funds in advance or by E-mandate
 In Zerodha, the current NACH-based Auto Add Funds system can result in ₹295 bounce charges if the bank balance is low, which makes many users hesitant to enable it.
 If Zerodha could bring:
 UPI AutoPay for adding funds, and
 Real-time deduction based on the actual SIP amount ( atleast approx amount is also great if you can )
 it would make stock SIPs much more convenient and safe for users like me.
Hope the team considers adding these features!

In the past 5 years, International mutual funds have become popular among retail investors. Up until 2016-17, we really didn’t have many options either, but in the last 2-3 years, we’ve seen several new global funds. But there are restrictions in terms of overseas investments. At an industry level, RBI has set the limit at $7 billion and this includes a $1 billion limit on overseas ETFs. At a fund level, SEBI had set a limit $1 billion for mutual funds and $300 million for overseas ETFs.
 Given the popularity of international mutual funds, the mutual fund industry is close to hitting the limits and all international mutual funds and ETFs have imposed various restrictions. The industry and SEBI are working with RBI to enhance the limits, but there’s nothing definitive yet.
 What does this mean for you as an investor? 
 We are getting queries from investors if they should cancel their SIPs and redeem their investments. This issue is purely related to the amount of money that the mutual fund industry can invest abroad, that’s it. This has no impact whatsoever on your SIPs and existing investments. Please continue investing as per your asset allocation.
 How does this impact my SIPs on Coin? 
 Most of the AMCs have stopped accepting fresh lumpsum and SIP registrations, but existing SIPs won’t be affected. Since we simulate SIPs on Coin with lumpsum investments , we’ll automatically migrate all monthly Coin SIPs in international mutual fund schemes to AMC SIPs by Feb 1st.
